2025 was filled with love. I played some sick shows to thousands of people, I got a Gold record for happy face and another Gold record for a song that I’m keeping secret for now… Id say overall it felt like a dismantling of everything I thought I knew. Never knew I knew how to dismantle an atom bomb until I did. When you’re inside it, it can feel like you’re stuck, or going backward, or that everything is crumbling. But looking back, it was all building something new. That’s what alchemy really is. Not magic. Just transformation happening slowly, under pressure.

I’m so grateful for the journey that led me here. For every moment that didn’t make sense while it was happening.

91 million streams on Spotify still doesn’t feel real. Thank you to everyone listening and sharing the music. Music has taken me around the world and into experiences and relationships that money could never buy. That alone has been the greatest gift of my life.

I started making music when I was young because I didn’t feel like I fit anywhere else. I felt too much. I saw too much. Music became the place where all of that had somewhere to go. Even now, there are moments I wish I could turn that sensitivity off. But it’s also the thing that lets me experience the world the way I do, and translate it into sound. I’m deeply grateful for that.

I’ve spent the last month in the Middle East creating a body of work that feels really special, and I’m excited to share it this next year.

Thank you to everyone who believed in me when I didn’t. To the people who talked sense into me when I felt like a failure. Who let me sleep on a couch. Who sent the random voice text. For the hugs (yeaaa I’m a hugger) This journey as an artist is wild but right now, maybe for the first time, I know I’m exactly where I’m supposed to be. 2026. Yeaaaa.

For anyone who needs to hear it. Keep going. There’s something inside you that needs to be expressed. The desires in your heart aren’t random. Your soul knows where you’re meant to go. If you listen, it will guide you...

I got dropped for this song.
Now it’s my first Gold record.

This is your reminder to trust yourself even when nobody else gets it. The label said this song would never work. They didn’t understand what I was doing. I was dropped and released it independently. For the first year and a half it didn’t stream well. It didn’t get playlists. It didn’t fit an algorithm or a genre. On paper it looked like a failure.

But people slowly found it. Shared it. Passed it around. It took time. And that’s the lesson. Not everything is meant to go viral right away. Some things need to time to grow. Sometimes the rest of the world needs to catch up with you. It can feel lonely at times. I’ve felt crazy, I’ve felt sad, but that thing that makes you different is often the thing you’re meant to protect. Not fix. Everyone has opinions. Everyone is right and wrong at the same time. The only voice you actually have to learn to listen to is your own inner compass.

Keep faith in yourself. Keep faith in God. Keep faith in the universe. Even when you can’t see the results yet, your belief is doing more than you think. Your thoughts, your heart, your vision are shaping reality in real time.

If you’ve been given a desire, a feeling, a calling in your soul, it isnt random. It was placed there by God for a reason. Trust it. Keep going. Learn how to see in the dark. 

Thank you to every single person who has believed in me, seen me, let me sleep on their couch, EVERYONE who has listened to Jagwar Twin and shared the music. What a beautiful way to end this year. Sending my love 🤍- Jag 🐆🌎

I’ve been thinking of the right words to say this for a while. ⁠
TikTok saved my life. Last year I turned 35 and I found myself as a struggling artist who couldn’t afford groceries or rent and had to move back in with my parents. At this point I had been making music seriously since I was 15. I had been signed and dropped by multiple major labels. Thank God almighty for Timothee Chalamet. In December of 2023 Bad Feeling blew up on TikTok with the release of the Wonka movie. It changed my life. I started making money, went on an arena tour with 30 Seconds to Mars, and most of all I got to connect with a bunch of weirdos and nerds who also connected with my music. I found people who see the world similarly to me. That has been the most rewarding part of this journey. There are so many people out there like me, with big dreams and at times the pursuit of something big can feel devastatingly lonely. At times along the way I questioned if I really had something special to offer the world or if I was just having an extended psychotic episode. But I got where I am now and I’m so grateful to be here.⁠
What I’m wanting to say in this long winded post is is thank you to everyone who has been there for me. And to everyone who saw me even before I did. I want to stay connected with the amazing humans I’ve met through Jagwar Twin, but I’ve also seen the negative effects in my life of spending so much time here on social media. I was spending 5-6 hours a day on social media making tiktoks, IG reels and stories, responding to comments and messages, and I had to ask myself why I was really doing it? On one level I love to connect p33ple. But on another, more subtle level I felt a desperate need to make “fans” and have people “like” my posts and me. I started to feel myself reaching for outside validation. My biggest fear used to be having to work some meaningless cubicle 9-5 job my whole life, but I realized social media is worse. It never turns off. You can be reached 24/7. You’re always making content. But I’m not content w...

Birthday notes 35 ⁠
⚡️🌲💀🌞✝️⁠
In the past I’ve felt pretty down on my birthday. Every new trip around the sun, I’d look at my life and see myself largely as a failure. I’d wish that more people listened to my music and that I was selling out massive tours around the world like so many of my friends, that I could afford my own place to live and all those kind of things that come with a “successful” music career. This year I’m turning 35. I still feel like I’m 18. I thought I would be retiring at 35, have a wife, maybe a couple kids and a long legacy music career in the rear view. Tonight Im sleeping at a Comfort Inn in Roswell New Mexico with a shower that doesn’t work, but there’s a double rainbow overhead, it’s Milky Way season and I’m on top of the world. ⁠
I am proud of Who I am. I’m strong, and brave, and compassionate, and see people, and I’m wiser than I was yesterday, forever learning. After this tour ends I don’t know where I’m going but as this huge lightning storm cracks on in the New Mexican sky I get the funny feeling that I’m exactly where I’m supposed to be. This will be the greatest year I have ever known. Thank you for being here.⁠
Greetings from Roswell and happy birthday to me⁠
- L7 Roy EL

I haven’t been posting on the social media web2 much lately but here’s my diary. Woke up at 5am and worked out first thing. It’s part of a new habit I picked up. It was cold and I didn’t want to but I did it anyway and that was a small victory. After that I did my rituals and then meditated listening to Temple Mind. I love Phil’s meditation music. A vivid memory came to me of my father carrying me around as an infant. In the memory I was crying because I was confused. Maybe because I was new to earth and I couldn’t do much because now I was a baby. Maybe I was used to being an infinity beam of light capable of anything. Idk. But my father took me out under the stars and I remember looking up at the heavens and I felt home again. I could hear the distant crashing waves of the ocean and feel the cold air on my cheeks. And most of all I could feel my father’s love for me and I knew that everything was going to be okay. Then I went to sleep. It’s wild the deep memories stored in our subconscious. They are always there. We are living and embodying them. Some beautiful like this. Some painful and often unseen. After that I hung out in web3 for a while. We’re about to see the new Renaissance in art and I feel blessed to be here and blessed to be creating what we are with Josh and Matt and Jon and Dan and the whole Cthdrl team. I went to the studio and worked on some interludes then painted because I used to love to paint as a kid. I read for an hour or so and practiced scales on the piano. I’m understanding music more the more I understand my self. I went on a hike later and Ash drove by while I was climbing up a hill with my 5sos merch headphones because I’m a super fan. Then I watched the sunset. After that I took a swim in the icy cold pool. Of course with my pink goggles. It hurt. But the jacuzzi felt good after. Now I’m guna make a pizza and probably listen to ABBA. Maybe Miles Davis. Idk. Seems like I did a lot when I write it but the days keep feeling shorter. I’m still trying to be like the sun. Diary - El Roy

When I was learning how to sing I would sing 8701 on repeat trying to figure out how to sound like him. I never figured that out, but it helped me find my own voice so thanks Usher. After that I trained with Rhys. Then I met up with Hudson for lunch. We ate ramen. After that I got ready to go to a friends show. I was checking the details and saw that they now required proof of vaccination for entry and the venue was no longer accepting a negative covid test for entry. I haven’t gotten the vaccine as of now so I let my friend know that I wasn’t going to be able to make it and wished them a beautiful show. I went on a run after that to the top of a hill at sunset and my mind starting thinking. If you have proof that you don’t have Covid shouldn’t that be fine? What am I missing? It’s still possible to get and spread Covid if you have been vaccinated, as far as I know, so my thinking was that everyone should provide a negative test regardless of vaccination. The choice is yours to make with whatever you do with your own body and you have to trust yourself with your unique mind/body/spirit.
